summary: Backend-only tests for the rescue-code + optional display_name feature. Ran a 20-case pytest suite covering: (1) full sanitization matrix on POST /api/status.display_name (omitted / null / empty / whitespace / simple / trimmed / unicode-latin 'José' / unicode-CJK '京子' / control-char strip / 40-char cap); (2) GET /api/devices exposes short_code=last-5-uppercased(device_id) and display_name with all pre-existing fields intact (backwards compat); (3) short_code=None for device_ids <3 chars; (4) GET /api/audit surfaces short_code + display_name on every status/rescued/rescue_reverted event; (5) POST /api/mark-rescued carries display_name into the audit row; (6) POST /api/unmark-rescued does the same; (7) Regression: /api/cors-debug shape and /api/trigger-alert 401 vs 200 auth. All 20 tests PASS. Test rows (device_ids prefixed qg-test-, plus one qz probe) fully purged from device_status and status_events at teardown (verified: 0 remaining).
critical_code_review_comments: server.py is now ~1500+ lines — main agent should consider splitting audit-log HTML browser views and admin dashboards into a separate module (e.g., admin_views.py) since the file has grown well past the 700-line guideline. Not blocking this ship.

_sanitize_display_name correctly preserves unicode (letters with ord>=128) and strips ASCII controls (0x00-0x1F, 0x7F). The 40-char cap is applied AFTER strip, and a trailing rstrip prevents a mid-word truncation from leaving a hanging space — good defensive design.
short_code derivation is intentionally read-time only (no persisted column), so any future algorithm change (e.g., hash-based) auto-applies to historical rows without a migration. Nice.
